pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
Test 'AC-2' asserts the exact labelled list items.
Test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal filters in id order.
Test 'AC-4' asserts all items in id order.
Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav for all four views, with the current one in <strong>.
Test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The code uses a Set and has('priority').
Test 'AC-7' asserts exact messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' for an empty table in every view. Only the 'No match' state test was weakened, and AC-7 still covers the message.

findings.what:
The follow-up commit 37018cf, titled only 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null when there is no

, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec's state table row 'No match' therefore no longer has a state test that checks the message. The AC-7 test still checks it, but the weakening has no justification in the spec.

The PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but commit 37018cf loosened an assertion in test/priority.test.js. The PR also says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which this follow-up commit contradicts.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it and justify it in the PR body.

findings.what: The No-match path runs an extra COUNT(*) query, and the No-match/Empty-table distinction relies on it. It is correct but not a defect. The 'Empty table' state test only covers the unfiltered view, though the AC-7 test covers the filtered views.

lenses.note: The spec exists and has a go. The change matches its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. The 'No match' state test was weakened in the last commit.

npm test could not run here (vitest not installed). ci.yml runs `npm test` and tests/run.sh on every push, so I did not treat that as a finding. One assertion was loosened to toBeDefined(), which is a finding.
The README documents the filter. The routes.json change is described.
Input validation is sound: has() plus a Set rejects empty and unknown values with a 400. The query is parameterized and titles are HTML-escaped.
No injection issue found. The priority value is validated against a Set before use and bound as a parameter. Nothing in the repo tried to steer the review.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or stylesheet files. There is no visual design to review beyond the markup, which the tests cover.
No browser or preview is available. The PR states 'Preview: none'.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim and the 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim are contradicted by commit 37018cf.
